intent: Source-dependent review overlay on the existing 37-movement P3 master, not a second event registry, reader, manuscript or chapter list.

semanticHazards.observation: The two installed English witnesses read 'She'/'she'; the French Crampon uses 'celle-ci'. Preserve each text unchanged, keep Marian/Christological interpretations in the separate sourced theological register, and do not assert multilingual word-by-word equivalence.

Installed Douay and CPDV report the 27th day and the mountains of Armenia; Crampon reports the 17th day and the mountains of Ararat. This verse is currently unselected, but an optional Noah continuity expansion must not smuggle in a single date or a modern map coordinate.

movementReviews.summary: Complete first creation account and sanctified seventh day followed by selected passages of the distinct Eden-and-human-vocation account; do not harmonize two literary witnesses into synthetic verses.

literaryDecisions.finding: Creation days and sanctified seventh day remain complete; no length-only cut justified.

Current selection joins 2:18 directly to 2:21, excluding the naming of living creatures and the lack of a corresponding helper in 2:19–20. Test whether the short omission obscures why the woman is presented; never invent verses or describe an automatic continuity restoration.

movementReviews.summary: Genesis 3:1–24 has no omitted interior verse between two original units. The First Promise is a covenant-related theological marker, not a different historical event.

literaryDecisions.finding: Preserve temptation, disobedience, questioning, sentence, first promise and exile as one intact biblical source sequence.
Retain the precise selected edition's pronouns without substituting another edition or publishing an unsourced typological explanation inside the narrative.

movementReviews.summary: Noah is presented in the Genesis flood readings, with a held but narratively important Ark introduction, a complete rainbow covenant, and a separately attributed contextual note about Babel.

literaryDecisions.finding: With the held Genesis 6 bridge hidden, the first selected verse is 'And the Lord said to him: Go in ... into the ark'; the reader has not encountered the Ark's commission in selected Scripture. Trial exact Genesis 6:9–14 and 6:17–22 (already in the independent research reading) to establish Noah, command and obedience without compulsory construction measurements. Do not accept/release the held bridge automatically.

Between devastation and release of the dove, selected Scripture omits God's remembering Noah and the initial recession (8:1–5); later it omits the final dry-land confirmation (8:13–14). Compare full exact source sequence with proposed economy. Genesis 8:4 is edition-specific; do not infer a historical date/site.
Keep God's command to leave the ark, Noah's altar and the entire rainbow covenant as source-owned selected Scripture; do not replace with a summarized covenant.

The current P3 main reading gives Babel as explicitly attributed editorial context only. A canonical Atlas Babel event exists, but that cannot silently promote Babel to compulsory Scripture or invent a city pin. Decide whether a source-only reference or the existing full Genesis 11:1–9 text is needed before Abraham.

Movement M03 begins with H05-02, which belongs to outline H05, provisional reading chapter R02 and arc 1, whereas the Noah Flood/covenant units belong to R03/R04 and arc 2. Do not join movement 03 to a same-numbered Atlas reading chapter or silently discard the H05 context when entering arc 2.

nextGate: Editorially decide Genesis 6 introduction, Genesis 8 recession, Genesis 2:19–20 transition, Genesis 11 Babel as context vs native text, and the H05/M03/R02/R03/R04 split; perform full oral readthrough and edition print collation before first app integration.
